claim: The mammary epithelium is a bilayer of two major phenotypically and functionally distinct cell lineages: luminal epithelial and myoepithelial cells.
source: The mammary epithelium is a bilayer of two major phenotypically and functionally distinct cell lineages: luminal epithelial and myoepithelial cells.
evidence: This is established knowledge about mammary gland structure, stated as a foundational fact in the abstract.

claim: Mammary luminal epithelia exhibit substantial stereotypical changes with age.
source: Mammary luminal epithelia exhibit substantial stereotypical changes with age that merit attention because these cells are the putative cells-of-origin for breast cancers.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data presented throughout the manuscript showing age-dependent changes in luminal epithelial cells.

claim: Luminal epithelial cells are the putative cells-of-origin for breast cancers.
source: Mammary luminal epithelia exhibit substantial stereotypical changes with age that merit attention because these cells are the putative cells-of-origin for breast cancers.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field of breast cancer biology.

claim: Age-dependent directional changes in gene expression were observed in addition to increased transcriptional variance with age.
source: In addition to age-dependent directional changes in gene expression, we observed increased transcriptional variance with age that contributed to genome-wide loss of lineage fidelity.
evidence: This is supported by differential expression and differential variability analyses presented in the results.

claim: Increased transcriptional variance with age contributed to genome-wide loss of lineage fidelity.
source: In addition to age-dependent directional changes in gene expression, we observed increased transcriptional variance with age that contributed to genome-wide loss of lineage fidelity.
evidence: This is demonstrated through differential variability analysis and its contribution to loss of lineage-specific expression.

claim: Age-dependent variant responses were common to both lineages.
source: Age-dependent variant responses were common to both lineages, whereas directional changes were almost exclusively detected in luminal epithelia and involved altered regulation of chromatin and genome organizers such as SATB1.
evidence: This is supported by differential variability analysis showing significant changes in both LEPs and MEPs.

claim: Directional changes were almost exclusively detected in luminal epithelia.
source: Age-dependent variant responses were common to both lineages, whereas directional changes were almost exclusively detected in luminal epithelia and involved altered regulation of chromatin and genome organizers such as SATB1.
evidence: This is demonstrated by differential expression analysis showing 471 DE genes in LEPs versus only 29 in MEPs.

claim: Age-dependent directional changes in luminal epithelia involved altered regulation of chromatin and genome organizers such as SATB1.
source: Age-dependent variant responses were common to both lineages, whereas directional changes were almost exclusively detected in luminal epithelia and involved altered regulation of chromatin and genome organizers such as SATB1.
evidence: This is supported by data showing SATB1 downregulation with age in LEPs and its role as a genome organizer.

claim: Epithelial expression variance of gap junction protein GJB6 increased with age.
source: Epithelial expression variance of gap junction protein GJB6 increased with age, and modulation of GJB6 expression in heterochronous co-cultures revealed that it provided a communication conduit from myoepithelial cells that drove directional change in luminal cells.
evidence: This is supported by differential variability analysis and experimental validation in co-culture experiments.

claim: Modulation of GJB6 expression in heterochronous co-cultures revealed that it provided a communication conduit from myoepithelial cells that drove directional change in luminal cells.
source: Epithelial expression variance of gap junction protein GJB6 increased with age, and modulation of GJB6 expression in heterochronous co-cultures revealed that it provided a communication conduit from myoepithelial cells that drove directional change in luminal cells.
evidence: This is demonstrated through shRNA knockdown experiments showing that reducing GJB6 in older MEPs prevented them from imposing an older biological age on younger LEPs.

claim: Age-dependent luminal transcriptomes comprised a prominent signal that could be detected in bulk tissue during aging and transition into cancers.
source: Age-dependent luminal transcriptomes comprised a prominent signal that could be detected in bulk tissue during aging and transition into cancers.
evidence: This is supported by GSEA analysis showing enrichment of LEP-specific age-dependent genes in bulk tissue and their predictive value for cancer.

claim: A machine learning classifier based on luminal-specific aging distinguished normal from cancer tissue and was highly predictive of breast cancer subtype.
source: A machine learning classifier based on luminal-specific aging distinguished normal from cancer tissue and was highly predictive of breast cancer subtype.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the elastic net ML model achieving high accuracy in classifying normal tissue and PAM50 subtypes.

claim: 82% of new breast cancers are diagnosed in women ≥ 50 y.
source: Furthermore, breast tissue provides an ideal model for studying aging-associated cancer susceptibility as 82% of new breast cancers are diagnosed in women ≥ 50 y (DeSantis et al., 2019).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: Directional changes in gene expression with age have been reported in whole breast tissue, including changes associated with biological processes involved in breast cancer.
source: Directional changes in gene expression with age have been reported in whole breast tissue, including changes associated with biological processes involved in breast cancer (Lee and Lee, 2017; Yau et al., 2007).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: Aging is associated with significant shifts in proportions of breast cell lineages, including epithelial and stromal populations.
source: However, aging is also associated with significant shifts in proportions of breast cell lineages, including epithelial and stromal populations (Benz, 2008; Garbe et al., 2012).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: Myoepithelial cells are basally located and contractile and have tumor suppressive properties.
source: MEPs are basally located and contractile and have tumor suppressive properties (Pandey et al., 2010).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: Luminal epithelial cells include subpopulations of estrogen receptor negative (ER-) secretory cells, which represent 80–95% of luminal cells in breast tissue, and ER positive cells (ER+).
source: Luminal epithelial cells (LEPs) are apically located and include subpopulations of estrogen receptor negative (ER-) secretory cells, which represent 80–95% of luminal cells in breast tissue, and ER positive cells (ER+) (Booth and Smith, 2006).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: Loss of lineage fidelity in breast epithelia is an aging phenomenon in which the faithfulness of expression of established lineage-specific markers diminishes with age without loss of the lineage-specificity of other canonical markers nor of the gross phenotypic and histological differences between LEPs and MEPs.
source: We previously demonstrated loss of lineage fidelity in breast epithelia as an aging phenomenon—in which the faithfulness of expression of established lineage-specific markers diminishes with age without loss of the lineage-specificity of other canonical markers nor of the gross phenotypic and histological differences between LEPs and MEPs (Miyano et al., 2017).
evidence: This is cited from the authors' previous work.

claim: 4,040 genes (23% of all genes analyzed) had highly significant lineage-specific differential expression in younger women.
source: Restricting analysis to genes that had strong lineage-specific bias (DE adj. p<0.001, absolute log2 fold change (abs(lfc)) ≥1), we found 4,040 genes (23% of all genes analyzed) with highly significant lineage-specific DE in younger women
evidence: This is directly reported from the differential expression analysis results.

claim: Of the 4,040 lineage-specific genes in younger women, 59% were LEP-specific and 41% were MEP-specific.
source: Of these genes, 59% were LEP-specific and 41% were MEP-specific.
evidence: This is directly reported from the differential expression analysis results.

claim: 3,345 genes had highly lineage-specific differential expression in older women.
source: In contrast, 3345 genes had highly lineage-specific DE in older women (Figure 1—source data 2B) and (Figure 1—source data 3B), of which 56% were LEP-specific and 44% were MEP-specific.
evidence: This is directly reported from the differential expression analysis results.

claim: Of the 3,345 lineage-specific genes in older women, 56% were LEP-specific and 44% were MEP-specific.
source: In contrast, 3345 genes had highly lineage-specific DE in older women (Figure 1—source data 2B) and (Figure 1—source data 3B), of which 56% were LEP-specific and 44% were MEP-specific.
evidence: This is directly reported from the differential expression analysis results.

claim: Loss of lineage-specific expression with age occurred genome-wide and was detected in 1,022 genes, a majority of which (65%) were LEP-specific genes.
source: Loss of lineage-specific expression with age occurred genome-wide and was detected in 1022 genes, a majority of which (65%) were LEP-specific genes.
evidence: This is directly reported from the analysis of genes losing lineage-specific expression with age.

claim: 76% of LEP-specific genes and 63% of MEP-specific genes had higher fold changes between lineages in younger cells compared to older cells.
source: We found that 76% of LEP-specific genes and 63% of MEP-specific genes had higher fold changes between lineages in younger cells compared to older cells (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is directly reported from the analysis of fold changes in lineage-specific expression.

claim: Within genes maintaining lineage-specific expression with age, 67% of LEP-specific genes and 54% of MEP-specific genes showed larger fold differences between LEPs and MEPs in younger women.
source: Indeed, within the subset of genes for which lineage-specific DE was maintained with age by significance threshold, the majority—67% of LEP-specific genes and 54% of MEP-specific genes—still showed larger fold differences between LEPs and MEPs in younger women (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is directly reported from the analysis of genes maintaining lineage-specific expression.

claim: 224 candidate lineage-specific ligand-receptor pairs were identified in young LEPs and MEPs.
source: Using published ligand-receptor pairs (LRPs) (Ramilowski et al., 2015), we identified 224 candidate lineage-specific LRPs in young LEPs and MEPs
evidence: This is directly reported from the ligand-receptor pair analysis.

claim: Loss of lineage fidelity with age led to disruption of 74 ligand-receptor pairs based on the loss of lineage-specific expression of ligands and/or their cognate receptors.
source: Loss of lineage fidelity with age led to disruption of 74 LRPs based on the loss of lineage-specific expression of ligands and/or their cognate receptors (Figure 2B, Figure 2—source data 1B).
evidence: This is directly reported from the ligand-receptor pair analysis.

claim: In LEPs, 471 genes were differentially expressed as a function of age, in contrast to only 29 differentially expressed genes in MEPs.
source: In LEPs, 471 genes were DE as a function of age, in contrast to only 29 DE genes in MEPs (adj. p<0.05) (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is directly reported from the age-dependent differential expression analysis.

claim: Only five genes showed age-dependent changes that were lineage independent, showing differential expression associated with age in both LEPs and MEPs.
source: Only five genes showed age-dependent changes that were lineage independent, showing DE associated with age in both LEPs and MEPs—LRRC4, PSORS1C1, and SCNN1B upregulated in older epithelia, and ZNF518B and ZNF521 downregulated in older epithelia (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A), thus leaving only 24 genes that changed with age exclusively in MEPs.
evidence: This is directly reported from the age-dependent differential expression analysis.

claim: Age-dependent differential upregulation (251 genes) and downregulation (220 genes) of LEP gene expression occurred at comparable frequencies.
source: Age-dependent differential upregulation (251 genes) and downregulation (220 genes) of LEP gene expression (adj. p<0.05) occurred at comparable frequencies (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is directly reported from the age-dependent differential expression analysis.

claim: In LEPs, 82% of the genes that were differentially expressed changed in a direction towards acquiring MEP-like patterns with age.
source: In LEPs, 82% of the genes that were DE changed in a direction towards acquiring MEP-like patterns with age (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is directly reported from the analysis of directional changes in gene expression.

claim: Fifty transcription factors showed age-dependent differential expression in LEPs and 4 transcription factors showed differential expression in MEPs.
source: Fifty TFs showed age-dependent DE in LEPs and 4 TFs showed DE in MEPs (adj. p<0.05); the majority of these TFs have known roles in breast cancer progression.
evidence: This is directly reported from the transcription factor analysis.

claim: Of the differentially expressed transcription factors in LEPs, 88% changed expression towards MEP-like expression in older LEPs.
source: Of the DE TFs in LEPs, 88% changed expression towards MEP-like expression in older LEPs (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is directly reported from the transcription factor analysis.

claim: Only 9% of the lineage-specific differential expression loss was attributable to age-dependent differential expression in either LEPs or MEPs.
source: We found that only 9% of the lineage-specific DE loss was attributable to age-dependent DE in either LEPs or MEPs (adj. p<0.05).
evidence: This is directly reported from the analysis of loss of lineage fidelity mechanisms.

claim: Genes with at least a two-fold change in differential expression due to age accounted for only 21% of the observed loss in lineage-specific expression.
source: Expanding our criteria to include genes with at least a two-fold change in DE due to age, we found that these age-related changes accounted for only 21% of the observed loss in lineage-specific expression.
evidence: This is directly reported from the analysis of loss of lineage fidelity mechanisms.

claim: Differential variability analysis identified 137 genes in LEPs and 128 genes in MEPs that had significant age-dependent differential variability.
source: Differential variability (DV) analysis identified 137 genes in LEPs and 128 genes in MEPs that had significant age-dependent DV (adj. p<0.05) (Figure 3F, Figure 3—source data 1C and D).
evidence: This is directly reported from the differential variability analysis.

claim: Genes that had two-fold increases in variances with age explained 27% of the observed loss of lineage-specific expression events.
source: Genes that had two-fold increases in variances with age explained 27% of the observed loss of lineage-specific expression events, on a par with the proportion (21%) explained by genes that had two-fold changes in DE.
evidence: This is directly reported from the analysis of loss of lineage fidelity mechanisms.

claim: Seventeen hallmark gene sets were significantly modulated in LEPs based on differential expression.
source: Seventeen hallmark gene sets were significantly modulated in LEPs (adj. p<0.05) based on DE (Figure 3H, top).
evidence: This is directly reported from the GSEA analysis.

claim: Twenty hallmark gene sets were significantly modulated in MEPs based on differential expression.
source: Twenty hallmark gene sets were significantly modulated in MEPs (adj. p<0.05) based on DE (Figure 3I, top).
evidence: This is directly reported from the GSEA analysis.

claim: Five gene sets were significantly modulated based on differential variability and were enriched in older LEPs.
source: Five gene sets were significantly modulated (adj. p<0.05) based on DV and were enriched in older LEPs (Figure 3H, bottom).
evidence: This is directly reported from the GSEA analysis.

claim: Seven gene sets were significantly modulated based on differential variability and enriched in older MEPs.
source: Seven gene sets were significantly modulated (adj. p<0.05) based on DV and enriched in older MEPs (Figure 3I, bottom).
evidence: This is directly reported from the GSEA analysis.

claim: Genes upregulated in younger LEPs were significantly enriched in tissue from younger women.
source: We found significant enrichment of differentially upregulated genes identified in young LEPs in tissue from younger women (adj. p=0.012) (Figure 5A)
evidence: This is directly reported from the GSEA analysis of bulk tissue.

claim: Genes upregulated in older LEPs were significantly enriched in tissue from older women.
source: and differentially upregulated genes identified in old LEPs in tissue from older women (adj. p=0.006) (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is directly reported from the GSEA analysis of bulk tissue.

claim: SATB1 was significantly downregulated in both LEPs and breast tissue of older relative to younger women.
source: SATB1 was significantly downregulated in both LEPs and breast tissue of older relative to younger women (adj. p<0.05) (Figure 5Ci–ii).
evidence: This is directly reported from the differential expression analysis.

claim: PAM50 Luminal A, Luminal B, and Her2-enriched breast cancer subtypes had the lowest expression of SATB1 relative to PAM50 Basal-like and Normal-like intrinsic subtypes.
source: In TCGA breast cancers (n=1,089), PAM50 Luminal A (LumA), Luminal B (LumB), and Her2-enriched (Her2) breast cancer subtypes had the lowest expression of SATB1 relative to PAM50 Basal-like (Basal) and Normal-like (Normal) intrinsic subtypes (post hoc Wilcoxon adj. p<0.0001) (Figure 5Ciii).
evidence: This is directly reported from the analysis of TCGA data.

claim: SATB1 was significantly downregulated in PAM50 LumA, LumB and Her2 breast cancers relative to their matched normal tissue.
source: Moreover, we found that for primary tumors that had matched normal tissue in TCGA (n=114 tumor and n=109 normal), SATB1 was significantly downregulated in PAM50 LumA, LumB and Her2 breast cancers relative to their matched normal tissue (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B)
evidence: This is directly reported from the analysis of TCGA data.

claim: 26 SATB1-target genes showed specific age-dependent differential expression in the LEP lineage.
source: Furthermore, 26 SATB1-target genes showed specific age-dependent DE in the LEP lineage (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D)
evidence: This is directly reported from the analysis of SATB1 target genes.

claim: 42 genes encoding for cell-surface junction proteins were modulated in LEPs and/or MEPs with age.
source: We found 42 genes were modulated in LEPs and/or MEPs with age (Lepage test p<0.05) (Figure 6A, Figure 6—source data 1B).
evidence: This is directly reported from the Lepage test analysis.

claim: ELF5 was downregulated in younger LEPs when co-cultured on apical surfaces of older MEPs for 10 days.
source: ELF5 was downregulated in younger LEPs when co-cultured on apical surfaces of older MEPs for 10 days (Figure 6D)
evidence: This is directly reported from the co-culture experiment results.

claim: When co-cultured on top of older MEP-shGJB6 relative to older MEP-shCtrl, LEPs maintained expression of ELF5 at higher levels.
source: When co-cultured on top of older MEP-shGJB6 relative to older MEP-shCtrl, LEPs maintained expression of ELF5 at higher levels (Figure 6F)
evidence: This is directly reported from the co-culture experiment with GJB6 knockdown.

claim: 98% of age-dependent differential expression and differential variability genes in LEPs were differentially expressed between PAM50 intrinsic subtypes.
source: Indeed, we found that 98% of age-dependent DE and DV genes in LEPs (580 of 589 genes in the TCGA cohort) were differentially expressed between PAM50 intrinsic subtypes (KW BH adj. p<0.05, post hoc Wilcoxon BH adj. p<0.05) (Figure 7—source data 1A and B).
evidence: This is directly reported from the analysis of TCGA data.

claim: The machine learning classifier distinguished normal from cancer tissue 100% and 93.3% of the time in the TCGA and GTEx/GSE81540 test sets, respectively.
source: In addition to accurately classifying PAM50 subtypes, LEP-specific aging biomarkers distinguished normal from cancer tissue 100% and 93.3% of the time, respectively, in the TCGA and GTEx/GSE81540 test sets.
evidence: This is directly reported from the machine learning model performance evaluation.

claim: 127 genes with scaled variable importance contribution ≥25% in predicting at least one class were identified in the machine learning model.
source: We identified 127 genes with scaled variable importance contribution ≥25% in predicting at least one class (Figure 8A, Figure 8—source data 1A); 18% of predictors derived from DV analysis.
evidence: This is directly reported from the machine learning model analysis.

claim: 18% of the top predictors in the machine learning model were derived from differential variability analysis.
source: We identified 127 genes with scaled variable importance contribution ≥25% in predicting at least one class (Figure 8A, Figure 8—source data 1A); 18% of predictors derived from DV analysis.
evidence: This is directly reported from the machine learning model analysis.

claim: Differential variability genes were strong predictors of PAM50 LumA, LumB, and Her2 subtypes and bore no strong predictive value for PAM50 Basal subtypes.
source: Of interest, our analysis of the predictive power of DE and DV genes at identifying PAM50 subtypes (Figure 8A) showed that DV genes were strong predictors (scaled variable contribution ≥25%) of PAM50 LumA, LumB, and Her2 subtypes and bore no strong predictive value for PAM50 Basal subtypes.
evidence: This is directly reported from the machine learning model analysis.

claim: Organisms, organs, and tissues exhibit stereotyped aging phenotypes that represent the integration of accumulated, stochastically incurred damages to individual cells.
source: Organisms, organs, and tissues exhibit stereotyped aging phenotypes that represent the integration of accumulated, stochastically incurred damages to individual cells that result in commonly understood hallmarks of aging (López-Otín et al., 2013; Todhunter et al., 2018).
evidence: This is cited from published literature on aging hallmarks.

claim: Age-associated directional changes in transcriptomes of whole tissues are well documented.
source: Age-associated directional changes in transcriptomes of whole tissues are well documented (de Magalhães et al., 2009; Glass et al., 2013; Peters et al., 2015; Volkova et al., 2005).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: Variance in gene expression between individuals arises in the contexts of tumors, diet, and aging.
source: Indeed, variance in gene expression between individuals arises in the contexts of tumors, diet, and aging (Bashkeel et al., 2019; Brinkmeyer-Langford et al., 2016; de Jong et al., 2019; Sharma et al., 2018; Viñuela et al., 2018).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: Cultured pre-stasis human mammary epithelial cells support growth of breast epithelial cell lineages from women across the lifespan.
source: Cultured pre-stasis human mammary epithelial cells (HMEC) support growth of breast epithelial cell lineages from women across the lifespan (Garbe et al., 2009; Labarge et al., 2013)
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: HMECs enable detailed, reproducible molecular studies of cancer progression.
source: and enable detailed, reproducible molecular studies of cancer progression (Stampfer et al., 2013).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: Mammary glands are bilayer structures consisting of Keratin 19 (KRT19)-positive LEPs surrounded by KRT14-positive contractile MEPs.
source: Mammary glands are bilayer structures consisting of Keratin 19 (KRT19)-positive LEPs surrounded by KRT14-positive contractile MEPs (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is established knowledge about mammary gland structure, supported by immunofluorescence imaging in Figure 1A.

claim: The luminal lineage is composed of ER+ hormone sensing and ER- secretory populations with ER- LEPs accounting for the vast majority of the luminal lineage independent of age.
source: The luminal lineage is composed of ER+ hormone sensing and ER- secretory populations with ER- LEPs accounting for the vast majority of the luminal lineage independent of age (Pelissier Vatter et al., 2018).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: Key lineage markers, including EPCAM and ERBB2 for LEPs, and TP63 and EGFR for MEPs, were differentially expressed in FACS-enriched LEPs and MEPs from HMEC primary cultures.
source: Key lineage markers, including EPCAM and ERBB2 for LEPs, and TP63 and EGFR for MEPs, were differentially expressed in FACS-enriched LEPs and MEPs from HMEC primary cultures as expected (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1E; Del Toro et al., 2024; Pandey et al., 2010; Thi et al., 2024).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1C and cited literature.

claim: KRT19 and KRT14 were exclusively expressed in CD133+/CD271- LEPs and CD133-/CD271+ MEPs, respectively.
source: We confirmed lineage-specific KRT protein expression by intracellular staining flow cytometry; KRT19 and KRT14 were exclusively expressed in CD133+/CD271- LEPs and CD133-/CD271+ MEPs, respectively (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1F.

claim: RNA-seq analysis identified 17,328 genes with comparable ranges of expression levels and consistent lineage-specific expression between primary organoid and 4th passage LEPs and MEPs in both age cohorts.
source: RNA-seq analysis identified 17,328 genes with comparable ranges of expression levels and consistent lineage-specific expression between primary organoid and 4th passage LEPs and MEPs in both age cohorts (linear regression R2=0.88–0.91, p<0.0001) (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–D).
evidence: This is supported by linear regression analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–D.

claim: Early passage primary HMECs in culture retained lineage specificity when compared to uncultured primary breast epithelial organoids.
source: Thus, early passage primary HMECs in culture retained lineage specificity when compared to uncultured primary breast epithelial organoids.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of gene expression between cultured and uncultured cells.

claim: Loss of lineage fidelity is the loss of faithful expression of lineage-specific markers with age, seen as shifts in distributions of fold changes between lineages to smaller values in the older cohort.
source: Loss of lineage fidelity is the loss of faithful expression of lineage-specific markers with age. Statistically, we described this loss as a phenomenon whereby the magnitude of gene expression differences that distinguish LEPs from MEPs decreased with age, which is seen as shifts in distributions of fold changes between lineages to smaller values in the older cohort (Kolmogorov-Smirnov two-sample test, KS p<0.0001) (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Loss of lineage fidelity led to enrichment of genes and biological processes commonly dysregulated in cancers.
source: Loss of lineage fidelity led to enrichment of genes and biological processes commonly dysregulated in cancers, and altered the LEP-MEP interactome that was significantly modulated by apical cell-cell junction proteins, such as GJB6.
evidence: This is supported by functional enrichment analysis and ligand-receptor pair analysis.

claim: Modulating GJB6 expression via shRNA in MEPs was sufficient to reduce the rate of molecular aging of adjacent LEPs as determined with a breast-specific biological clock.
source: Modulating GJB6 expression via shRNA in MEPs was sufficient to reduce the rate of molecular aging of adjacent LEPs as determined with a breast-specific biological clock.
evidence: This is supported by co-culture experiments with GJB6 knockdown.

claim: Genes that had age-dependent directional and variable changes in normal LEPs had predictive value in distinguishing normal breast tissue from breast cancers and in classifying breast cancer PAM50 subtypes.
source: Using machine learning, we showed that genes that had age-dependent directional and variable changes in normal LEPs had predictive value in distinguishing normal breast tissue from breast cancers and in classifying breast cancer PAM50 subtypes.
evidence: This is supported by machine learning model performance.

claim: Age-dependent changes in LEPs reflected dysregulation of biological processes that are convergent with breast cancer.
source: Age-dependent changes in LEPs reflected dysregulation of biological processes that are convergent with breast cancer.
evidence: This is supported by GSEA and functional enrichment analyses.

claim: The degree and variability of age-dependent changes across individuals may explain the differential susceptibility between individuals to breast cancer initiation, and to the development of specific breast cancer subtypes.
source: The degree and variability of age-dependent changes across individuals may explain the differential susceptibility between individuals to breast cancer initiation, and to the development of specific breast cancer subtypes.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the integration of all findings.

claim: Luminal epithelia are the ultimate site of integration of the variant responses to aging in their surrounding tissue.
source: We speculate that luminal epithelia are the ultimate site of integration of the variant responses to aging in their surrounding tissue, and that their emergent phenotype both endows cells with the ability to become cancer-cells-of-origin and represents a biosensor that presages cancer susceptibility.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the findings.

claim: The emergent phenotype of luminal epithelia endows cells with the ability to become cancer-cells-of-origin and represents a biosensor that presages cancer susceptibility.
source: We speculate that luminal epithelia are the ultimate site of integration of the variant responses to aging in their surrounding tissue, and that their emergent phenotype both endows cells with the ability to become cancer-cells-of-origin and represents a biosensor that presages cancer susceptibility.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the findings.
